content.comment_body: Hello everyone, I'm encountering an unusual issue with the latest [product_name] [version_no]. I use several on-delay timers whose values come from an up/down counter, initially set to 180. The counter's output is connected to the timer. Everything works at first, but after I close my project, exit [product_name] and reopen it, the connections appear lost. The counter's value doesn't reach the timer anymore—it reads as 0. Uploading the program to the device also fails. I have to remove and recreate each connection for it to work. It's quite frustrating! Might this behavior be due to separating my connections to keep the project organized?

This issue with splitting compounds for analog signals was already raised back in 2014 on the German forum. If I were you, I'd always minimize the parameter fields and close the reference lines. That way, the project stays organized and the reference lines remain intact.
Thanks for the info. I've noticed that if I save the project in .BIN format (for SD card up/download), the connections don't break. For now, I'll use this method. Best regards, [user_name]

analysis.insight_summary: Users report an issue in [product_name] [version_no]: connections between counters and on-delay timers disconnect after saving, closing, and reopening the project or software, causing logic to malfunction and requiring manual reconnection. This undermines workflow efficiency and trust in project reliability.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect logic and connections created and saved in [product_name] to remain intact and functional after closing and reopening the software, and to operate correctly when downloaded to the [product_name] hardware.
